name: Hollywood Garbage
description: Hollywood Garbage (also known as Junk Poker or Garbage) is a multi-phase social gambling game played with a massive deck (often 2-3 standard decks). It combines elements of Poker, Bingo, and simple card-matching. It is designed for large groups and operates through a sequence of phases that slowly deplete a shared pot of coins or chips.
deck: 2 standard 52-card decks (4-5 players); 3 or more decks (6+ players), shuffled together

history.origins: A traditional American 'parlor' game, likely emerging in the mid-20th century as a more complex version of simple matching games for small stakes.
timeline: Mid-20th Century: Popularized in social clubs and home games.
Present: Remains a common game for multi-deck casual play with pennies or small change.
history.cultural: Commonly played during long social gatherings where the goal is entertainment over a long period rather than high-stakes gambling.
history.evolution: The name 'Hollywood' probably reflects its multi-phase scoring structure, similar to Hollywood Gin.

setup.deck: 2 decks (4-5 players) or 3+ decks (6+ players). Shuffled together.
setup.dealing: The dealer deals 5 cards face up to each player.

rules.objective: Each hand has four phases: (1) Poker—ante, deal 5 face-up, best hand wins pot; (2) Bingo—dealer calls ranks, players put coins on matching cards, first with all five covered wins coins on cards; (3) Put and Take—dealer turns 10 then 10 cards, players put then take coins by rank; (4) Count-Up—dealer turns 13 cards counting ace to king, players pay dealer when rank matches position. Deal passes left after each hand.
rules.gameplay: Everyone antes. Dealer shuffles and deals 5 cards face up to each player. Best poker hand wins the pot (ties share). Same five cards stay; dealer turns undealt cards one by one calling rank; players with that rank put a coin on each matching card; first to have a coin on all five calls Bingo and wins all coins on everyone's cards. Phase 3: dealer discards own hand and called cards; turns 10 cards—players put 1, 2, … 10 coins per match into pot; then 10 more—players take 1, 2, … 10 per match; remainder to dealer. Phase 4: dealer deals 13 face-up counting ace to king; when turned rank matches count, everyone pays dealer that many coins (J=11, Q=12, K=13). Hand over; next player deals.
keyRules: Phase 1: Standard poker hand ranking; best five-card hand wins ante pot; ties split.
Phase 2: First player to place a coin on all five of their cards calls Bingo and wins all coins on the table; multiple winners share.
Phase 3: Put and Take uses the same 1–10 then 1–10 coin structure; dealer covers shortfall or keeps remainder.
Phase 4: Count-Up (Birthday): dealer collects when turned card rank matches its position in the ace-through-king count.

strategy.basic: Since cards are dealt face-up, Phase 1 is pure luck. Strategy is restricted to side-betting if allowed.
strategy.intermediate: In Phase 2, tracking which cards have been called helps you know how close your opponents are to calling 'Bingo'.
strategy.advanced: Social engineering: In games with larger pots, betting on and encouraging specific dealers can affect the pool, though the mechanics are mostly deterministic once cards are dealt.
tips: Use pennies or low-value chips; the amount of coins on the cards can grow quickly.
The 'Best Hand' in Phase 1 is often a pair or two-pair given the large card pool.

variations.name: Four-flush in Poker
variations.description: A four-flush (four cards of one suit) beats a pair but loses to two pairs in the poker phase.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant only changes hand ranking in poker phase; no engine overrides needed yet.

scoring.description: Winner of Poker rounds + Bingo wins entire hand.
scoring.winCondition: First to Bingo or highest poker hand.

synthesis.shortDescription: A hybrid game combining poker hands and bingo patterns.
